home-p-2: I am passionate about engine design and rocket propulsion, with interests spanning aircraft design and engineering analysis.
frl-p-3: Independently completed preliminary design for a pressure-fed LOX/IPA engine, connecting sizing, feed systems, injector design, ignition, nozzle analysis, bolted-joint calculations, and preliminary heat-transfer analysis.
frl-figcaption-0: SolidWorks engine assembly. Contains the combustion chamber, conical nozzle, coaxial swirl injector, ASI, sealing mechanisms, and eight bolts surrounding the flanges with washers and nuts attached.
frl-p-4: Produced a preliminary engine design adhering to the mission requirements, with all geometry backed by calculations and educated estimates of correction factors.
solar-p-3: A study of solar-cell temperature under prescribed irradiance levels, connecting CAD, ANSYS steady-state thermal simulation, and MATLAB post-processing.
solar-figcaption-0: 72-cell panel CAD model created in SolidWorks. Contains solar cells with busbars and fingers, encapsulants, back sheets, a glass wall, and a frame.
solar-figcaption-2: ANSYS temperature result across the modeled assembly.
solar-li-1: Used the single-cell model for a ANSYS steady-state thermal analysis within available mesh limits.
solar-p-4: Incorporated all the new software taught to me during my first year at the university (SolidWorks, MATLAB, and ANSYS), enhancing my technical skill in each. Through the project, I established a workflow for varying irradiance inputs and compared simulated temperature and heat-flux results.
uav-h3-0: UAV Tail Design and Airfoil Analysis
uav-figcaption-1: Exploded tail assembly showing the interfaces of the components.
uav-figcaption-2: XFLR5 airfoil study used for airfoil selection of the stabilizers.
uav-li-2: Contributed to the team’s terrain-mapping UAV design and researched tapered-wing and construction-material trade-offs such as Carbon fiber, fiberglass, and Balsa wood.
iam3d-figcaption-0: Four-propeller VTOL drone CAD assembly, done in Autodesk Fusion
iam3d-figcaption-1: The finalized 3D printed VTOL drone, in orange and blue for UF.
iam3d-p-4: Produced a functionable VTOL drone flown with a remote control.
leadership-figcaption-0: Aircraft designed by one of the new-member teams. Each member worked toward their respective part; assembly includes fuselage, landing gear, wings, nose cone, and tail components.
leadership-li-0: Taught aerodynamic fundamentals to new members and SolidWorks and Fusion workflows.
leadership-li-1: Guided teams in coordinating component dimensions and assembly interfaces.
leadership-p-4: Mentored two new-member teams through their aircraft design work. Met with them weekly to benefit each member's growth.
about-p-1: I’m studying Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Florida, with graduation expected in May 2028. I earned my Associate of Arts and High School Diploma simultaneously through the program of College Academy at Broward College in May 2025.
about-p-2:
I really enjoy learning anything that has to do with aerospace, which is why most of my work is reading textbooks and research on the subject. Incorporating the things I learn from literature into real designs is what I love doing and am proud of the work that I do.

Apart from the technical side of things, I also have other hobbies. My favorite thing to do is play futbol, I've been playing it my whole life. Music is also a big part of my life, and I enjoy playing the piano, guitar, and drums. To keep a healthy lifestyle, I also go to the gym everyday to get some exercise in. Lastly, I enjoy playing video games (Just not during the school semester).
leadership-li-3: Helped translate mass, volume, payload, and endurance requirements into energy estimates and motor and battery choices.
leadership-li-2: Taught members how to use ANSYS Fluent to analyze lift and drag of the aircraft to get a functional design.
